$comment: Acceptance criteria for issue 191. Most of what a Copilot cloud-agent install needs already exists: .agents/skills is install-skill.sh:28's default and one of the three paths Copilot reads; SKILL.md carries exactly the required frontmatter, name (lowercase-hyphen) and description, and nothing else; ADR-011's zero dependencies mean Python 3 in the runner has nothing to install; gh and a token are already in the environment so admission='milestone' needs no configuration. What is missing is documentation and two declared decisions. THIS BAR COVERS THE MECHANISM AND NOT THE EVIDENCE, and says so in 'covers' rather than in prose -- two earlier bars recorded their scope in a comment and both read STOP_COMPLETE for work that was half undone (issue 133). Copilot chooses skills 'based on your prompt and the skill's description', the same pull-based description-matched mechanism as Claude Code, where Arm A stands at 0 FULL / 1 PARTIAL / 2 NONE / 1 AMBIGUOUS over four prompts. Nothing in this issue improves that number and nothing here should claim to. THE DECISION THAT MUST NOT DRIFT: allowed-tools ships UNSET. GitHub's own documentation warns it removes the confirmation step, and a skill that runs shell without asking is a posture the installing repository declares, not one this project assumes on its behalf. C1 is a check that it stays unset -- the easiest thing in this issue to 'helpfully' add later.

covers.declared: the mechanism -- a documented, opt-in install path for the Copilot cloud agent, with allowed-tools left unset and no hook installed automatically
covers.uncovered: whether the skill activates on that host. Copilot's discovery is description-matched, identical in kind to the mechanism issue 5 measures, and no arm of docs/research/activation-protocol.md has been run against Copilot. Documenting an install path is not evidence that governance reaches the model.
covers.split_note: NO split_to. The activation arm was not split out of this work -- it is the same shape as issues 36 and 37 and belongs with them under RG-VALIDATION, gated on access to the host rather than on anything here.

criteria.$comment: C1 THE DECISION THAT MUST HOLD. allowed-tools stays out of SKILL.md's frontmatter. Green today and it must stay green -- this is a control against a future convenience, not a defect to fix.
C2 the host table names the Copilot cloud agent and the paths it reads, so a reader is not left to infer it from .agents/skills being cross-vendor.
C3 the allowed-tools line is DOCUMENTED with its argument and its risk, not merely omitted. An undocumented omission is indistinguishable from an oversight, and the next person adds it.

C4 nothing installs automatically. The installer must not offer or write a hook for the cloud agent, which has no prompt-submit surface of its own -- and must say so, the way it already does for Codex.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/install.py | grep -q "\[PASS\].*no hook is offered for the cloud agent"'

criteria.$comment: C5 THE CLAIM THIS MUST NOT MAKE. No document may report an activation result for Copilot, because none has been run. conformance/skill.py already fails an unmarked claim of this shape; this criterion states it for the host.
criteria.target: bash -c '! grep -rniE "copilot.*(verified|activation rate|FULL activation)" docs/ README.md'
